deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a continuous German prose passage of historical lecture or school notes on ancient Syracuse. It continues the 'Periodisierung' from folio 68: '3 Periode. Von der Vertreibung Thrasybuls bis auf die Erhebung Dionysius I, 466–405'. The content, in order:
(1) After Thrasybulus was expelled (466 BC), Syracuse regained its freedom and a democracy. The city grew and gradually became the head of all the colonies in Sicily. 'Großgriechenland' is struck through and replaced by 'Sicilien'.
(2) Disputes arose on Sicily. Agrigent resisted, and in 416 a war followed in which the Syracusans held their ground.
(3) The great struggle with Athens, 415–413 (the Sicilian Expedition). It looked dangerous but became 'der Grund zu ihrer Größe'. The Athenians besieged Syracuse, but with Spartan help Syracuse gained the upper hand, besieged and enclosed the Athenians, and won.
(4) In 412 Syracuse received a lawgiver named Diocles.
(5) In 410 the quarrels between Segesta and Selinus led to war with Carthage. Segesta called on the Carthaginians, who advanced so far that Syracuse itself became alarmed. The Syracusans took countermeasures and appointed generals, among them a young man, Dionysius, 'der alle Eigenschaften eines Demagogen hatte, und sich der Herrschaft bemächtigen wollte'. The narrative continues on folio 70 with Dionysius's seizure of power in 405.
The surrounding pages (68, 70) are the same history notes. There are no derivations, formulas, or computations to reconstruct. The page number '69' in the upper right corner is the only numeral besides the historical dates (BC).
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematics. Historical note: the dating 'Agrigent ... 416' is doubtful. The well-known Syracuse–Akragas war was c. 446/445 BC. The conflict of 416 BC was between Segesta and Selinus, and it prompted the Athenian expedition of 415. The 410 entry (Segesta–Selinus, Carthaginian intervention) is close to the usual 410/409 BC.
The Athenian siege of Syracuse ended in 413 BC with the Athenian defeat, consistent with the notes. Diocles as lawgiver c. 412 BC matches Diodorus.

results.what: Historical lecture or school notes on the history of Syracuse (democracy after 466 BC, Athenian expedition 415–413, Diocles 412, Carthaginian war 410, rise of Dionysius I).

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely historical prose about ancient Syracuse, likely student or lecture notes bound into the bundle. It contains no mathematical content, so there is nothing that could be attributed to Gauss as a mathematical result.
transcription_corrections: Line 2–3: 'Die Nachbarstaaten[?] sahen zu und wurden allmählich das Haupt' should most likely read 'Die Stadt nahm sehr zu und wurde allmählich das Haupt von allen Kolonien'. This matches the image and the sense: the city, not neighbouring states, became the head.

'die beiden[?] Hülfe der Sparter' is likely just 'durch die Hülfe der Sparter'. The struck-through words 'Athen oder die beiden' precede it, and the subject that 'erhielt das Uebergewicht' is Syrakus.

The insertion above 'belagerte' reads 'die Athener'. The struck word below appears to be 'Athener' or 'Athenienser'. The phrase 'in [...] eingeschlossen' seems to be a correction of 'in Verschanzungen'-type wording, with 'ferner' interlined, followed by '...hatten'. It remains uncertain.
'Die machten Gegenanstalten' is probably 'Sie machten Gegenanstalten'. The image shows 'Gegenanstalten' with an interlinear 'r' correction.
'Dionysius[?]' is confirmed as 'Dionysius' by context and by the next page.
